subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB525 + PB526 LANDED - THE EXCEPTION CONDITION IS AN EXCEPTION CONDITION. The timing half was already right and still is (GR6 a) a literal's value is always that literal; GR6 b) 1 read at the completion of OPEN OUTPUT; GR6 b) 2 re-read during a WRITE ADVANCING PAGE; GR6 b) 3 re-read during a page-overflow WRITE, after the overflow decision was taken against the OLD body; 'the value applies to the next logical page'). WHAT LANDED is the whole second half. (i) Both VALUE RULES are now enforceable and enforced: GR6 b) 1 'The page size shall be greater than zero' and GR6 b) 2 'The footing start shall be greater than zero and not greater than the page size' - the latter applied exactly when the FOOTING PHRASE IS SPECIFIED, which required making the absent phrase ABSENT in the model (LinagePage.Footing is int?, SequentialIoEmitter.LinageOpExpr renders null for an omitted phrase) instead of encoding it as the value 0. (ii) A violation is no longer a raw System.InvalidOperationException that kills the process: EvaluateLinage returns false and the connector reports an unsuccessful I-O status '90' (§9.1.13.11's implementor-defined value; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 DOC-A.1-110) together with the exception-name GR6 b) 2 NAMES, through FileConnector.SetIoCondition - and the raise itself goes through the ONE EC-I-O channel, the emitted __IoCheckEc hook, which owns the USE format-1 and format-3 tiers, the exception-checking PERFORM frames and the fatal default. The name has to travel beside the status because §9.1.13.1's status->EC correspondence has no entry for EC-I-O-LINAGE and reads a '9x' as EC-I-O-IMP; §14.6.13.1.1's 'Unless otherwise specified, if more than one exception is detected during the execution of a statement, the one that is set to exist is undefined' is the licence for the specific rule to win, and FileRegistry.IoConditionName is the ONE place the named condition and the correspondence are combined. (iii) ALL THREE consequences of GR6 b) 2's closing sentence are realized and witnessed: execution continues with the statement following the WRITE (measured: the DISPLAY after the failing WRITE runs); the LINAGE-COUNTER is set to 0 and remains at that value until the file is closed (measured: LC=000 at the violation, at every later WRITE, and back to 001 only after a CLOSE + fresh OPEN OUTPUT); and all subsequent WRITE statements referencing the file cause the condition to continue to exist until the file is closed (the _linagePageBroken latch, checked by BOTH write entries because a plain WRITE on a LINE SEQUENTIAL LINAGE file does not route through WriteAdvancing). The file connector STAYS OPEN at an OPEN-time violation - GR6 b) 2's 'until the file is closed' and 'all subsequent WRITE statements referencing the file' both presuppose it - so the OPEN reports the status and nothing else about it changes. With checking for EC-I-O-LINAGE enabled the standard fatal protocol applies unchanged (§14.6.13.1.3 4)-7)): 2023/pb526_linage_ec_checking runs a format-3 USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O-LINAGE declarative whose FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS reads EC-I-O-LINAGE (not EC-I-O-IMP - that is the assertion the name override exists for) and RESUMEs; with no handler the run unit terminates abnormally with a named diagnostic instead of a CLR stack dump. The 85 twin exists because the whole behaviour is reachable with no construct newer than 1985 - the status and the format-1 declarative carry it - so a regression making it depend on the EC subsystem being present cannot stay green.
